sources: Format watch (yt_scout formulas, 1116 videos over 100K from 54 searches) + spread on the survivors + this month's car/engineering/F1 searches. Numbers read 22 Oct 2026.
headline: The survival ladder just crossed six niches in three weeks. Cars have not touched it.
lede: Round 2 of the format lab. The headline is one format, not ten: How Long You'd Last in Every [X] put 96% of its lifetime views inside the last month, across prehistoric oceans, ice ages, dinosaurs, iPhones, FNAF and ACOTAR. No car video uses it. Three established formats follow as backups, each with its car crossing checked.

formats.niche: Nature / survival. Copied within three weeks into ice ages, dinosaurs, FNAF, an iPhone century and ACOTAR courts.
formats.formula: How Long You'd Last in Every [place / era / set]
formats.thumbnail: One creature or vehicle on a flat coloured ground, the title across the top in heavy caps with the survival time as the promise; no face, no arrow, no red circle.
formats.structure: A ladder of entries. Each entry: name it, place the viewer in it, count the seconds or hours you survive, move on. A running score makes the next entry inevitable.
formats.visual: Flat 2D diagrams on a single colour field: silhouettes, cutaway anatomy, a scale object (a bus) next to the animal. Simple shape tweening, no footage, no presenter.

merges.audience: F1 story viewers and explainer viewers. F1 story videos clear 300K to 900K this month from small channels (Evolution of F1 Cars 316K, Disrespectful Moments 465K), and the diagram look is the proven look of the format we are borrowing.
merges.proven: The claim formula is established and still working: 23 of 29 videos over 100K this month, including one from a 15K-subscriber channel at 930K. The diagram look carries 2.9M in the same month.
merges.unproven: No F1 video uses either half together. The 1994 facts are the film's risk: every claim must be sourced before the script is written.
